html:
The Lucayans were the Taino people of the Bahamas, who settled the islands more than a thousand years ago, coming from Cuba and Hispaniola. They fished, farmed cassava and traded by canoe.

On 12 October 1492 Columbus landed on one of their islands, which they called Guanahani and he named San Salvador. He wrote that they were gentle and would make good servants.

Within a few decades the Spanish carried off the Lucayans as slaves to work in the mines of Hispaniola and the pearl beds off Venezuela. By about 1520 the islands were empty. The Bahamas stayed unsettled until the Eleutheran Adventurers came from Bermuda in 1648.
